title: Kim’s Second Byungjin: 21 Years After the Six-Party Talks Agreement
summary_en: North Korea is pursuing a “second byungjin” that advances its nuclear program while also seeking to normalize relations with countries willing to tolerate (if not necessarily accept) North Korea as a nuclear power.

title: The Melting Arctic Lifeline for Russia’s Shadow Fleet
summary_en: Two floating storage vessels have handled an estimated 53 percent of Russia’s seaborne Arctic crude exports since February 2022. CSIS Futures Lab analysis shows how the United States and Europe can target these bottlenecks to constrain the Kremlin’s wartime revenue.
title_cn: The Melting Arctic Lifeline for Russia’s Shadow Fleet

title: Is Venezuela Moving Toward Democracy?
summary_en: More than nine months after the capture of Nicolás Maduro, CSIS Americas Program Acting Director and Senior Fellow Christpher Hernandez-Roy and Antonella Navarro assess Venezuela's progress towards political transition.

title: Project Vault Moves from Concept to Execution
summary_en: Project Vault is moving from concept to execution. Glencore and Mercuria are committing $1 billion to source and stockpile critical minerals for U.S. manufacturers, putting the United States’ first commercial strategic minerals reserve into motion.
